title: Tamsin and the Spire
premise: Edmund Coldharbour, exiled storm-caller and smuggler, is guiding a desperate client through the Thornfell mountains when the border wards collapse and the stars go out — the work of the Spire, the court beneath the mountain that buys souls to fuel its endless night. The client, Tamsin, reveals she sold her younger brother's soul to the Spire years ago to survive a famine winter, and now means to steal it back before his debt comes due at the turning of the year. Edmund, whose own exile stems from refusing to call storms for the old king's wars, must choose between the neutral roads he has kept for twenty years and a justice no court will grant. Together they descend through smuggler tunnels, bargain with wardens of the dark, and confront the Spire's broker — who turns out to be the one who taught Edmund his craft. In the end Edmund spends his storm-gift to shatter the Spire's ledger, freeing every soul it holds but losing his magic forever; Tamsin carries her brother home into a dawn where stars return, and justice, bought at last outside any law.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who live in the gaps between laws.

chapters.title: The Last Lit Road
chapters.summary: Edmund Coldharbour guides a paying client, Tamsin Vane, along a smuggler's pass through Thornfell, trading dry observations while she asks too many questions about the border wards. His POV establishes his exile, his rules, and his loneliness. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking an old grief he refuses to name.

chapters.title: When the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: At a high camp, the border wards fail with a sound like breaking glass and every star vanishes at once. Edmund realizes the wards were anchored to starlight — and something beneath the mountain has swallowed both. Tamsin's POV reveals her terror and her hidden purpose. Beat: awe curdling into dread as the world goes dark.

chapters.title: A Debt in Winter
chapters.summary: Trapped by the darkness, Tamsin confesses: seven years ago she sold her brother Wren's soul to the Spire's brokers to buy food through the famine. The debt comes due at midwinter — three weeks away. Edmund's POV; he wants to walk away. Beat: guilt laid bare, and the first crack in his neutrality.

chapters.title: The Broker's Mark
chapters.summary: They find a waystation defaced with the Spire's sigil and a warden's corpse, drained of warmth. Edmund recognizes the handiwork of Master Corvane, the broker who once trained him in storm-craft before his exile. Tamsin's POV. Beat: the past reaching up to seize the present.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Law
chapters.summary: Edmund takes Tamsin to Hollowmere, a smuggler haven under the eaves, hoping to buy passage or information. The haven's matriarch, Old Sable, refuses: no one crosses into Spire territory and returns. Edmund's POV. Beat: frustration and the sting of debts owed to Sable herself.

chapters.title: What Sable Knows
chapters.summary: Sable relents when Tamsin offers the only coin she has left — her own name, freely given, which the Spire values above gold. Sable maps the drowned stair, the only unguarded entrance. Tamsin's POV. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of what survival costs, again.

chapters.title: The Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: Descent through flooded tunnels lit by Edmund's failing storm-light. They encounter a lost child of the dark — a soul-fragment the Spire discarded — who leads them deeper in exchange for warmth. Edmund's POV. Beat: tenderness unexpected, and the first proof the Spire wastes what it buys.

chapters.title: Wardens of the Dark
chapters.summary: Captured by the Spire's wardens, faceless keepers who trade in silence, they are brought before a gate that reads souls like ledgers. Tamsin's mark admits them; Edmund's exile brands him twice over. Tamsin's POV. Beat: claustrophobic fear, and shame at being known.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: The Spire revealed: an inverted tower descending into stone, its halls lit by caged souls, its court presided over by the Broker Corvane. Edmund sees his old teacher enthroned. Edmund's POV. Beat: recognition and revulsion — the man he might have become.

chapters.title: An Old Bargain Reopened
chapters.summary: Corvane offers Edmund reinstatement: his exile lifted, his storms restored, if he delivers Tamsin and lets Wren's debt stand. He claims the famine was engineered to harvest souls — and that Edmund's king knew. Tamsin's POV. Beat: temptation sharpened by righteous fury.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Given quarters, they infiltrate the ledger vault where every sold soul is written. They find Wren's page — and discover his debt can be transferred, but only to a willing soul of equal weight. Edmund's POV. Beat: hope with a knife hidden inside it.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin resolves to substitute her own soul for her brother's, arguing she sold him once already and owes him this. Edmund, against every rule he keeps, refuses to let her. Tamsin's POV. Beat: love as debt, and the refusal to pay it that way.

chapters.title: Storms Remembered
chapters.summary: Edmund tells Tamsin the truth of his exile: he refused to call a storm on a starving village, and the king stripped his name. Corvane signed the order. His neutrality was never peace — it was scar tissue. Edmund's POV. Beat: confession as thawing; trust kindled.

chapters.title: The Turning Approaches
chapters.summary: Midwinter nears; the Spire's halls brighten as harvested souls are readied for consumption. The discarded child-soul warns them the ledger can be unmade only at the moment of the turning, when all debts come due at once. Tamsin's POV. Beat: ticking clock made visible.

chapters.title: Corvane's Lesson
chapters.summary: Corvane corners Edmund privately, revealing he arranged the famine not for the old king but for the Spire itself — he serves the hunger below, and always has. He offers Edmund partnership in the new dark. Edmund's POV. Beat: betrayal of betrayals; the mentor fully unmasked.

chapters.title: Allies in the Cages
chapters.summary: The caged souls, hearing Edmund's storm-heart, begin to hum in resonance. Old Sable arrives leading smugglers through the drowned stair — she never intended to abandon them. Tamsin's POV. Beat: solidarity rising from the margins; the lawless choosing each other.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Year
chapters.summary: At midwinter midnight the Spire opens its ledger to collect. Edmund calls the storm he swore off — not rain, but the memory of every storm, channeled through the resonating souls. Climax begins. Edmund's POV. Beat: sacrifice embraced; power spent like blood.

chapters.title: The Shattered Ledger
chapters.summary: The storm breaks the vault; pages burn free and every written soul tears loose. Corvane, clinging to his own contract, is claimed by the hunger he fed. Edmund's gift gutters out forever as the last page burns. Edmund's POV. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Among the freed souls, Tamsin finds Wren — older than he should be, hollowed but himself. He does not remember being sold, only waiting. Their reunion is quiet, imperfect, real. Tamsin's POV. Beat: grief and joy in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: The Spire collapses inward as its hunger starves; the company climbs the drowned stair as water rises behind them. Sable's smugglers carry the weakest freed souls. Tamsin's POV. Beat: exhausted, hard-won escape; the dark letting go.

chapters.title: Stars Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Above ground, the stars return one by one. Edmund, magicless for the first time since childhood, feels the silence where storms lived — and finds it bearable, because he chose it. Edmund's POV. Beat: mourning transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Spring: Tamsin and Wren farm the valley she once fled; Sable's routes now carry freed souls home instead of contraband. Edmund stays on as a guide with no gift but his knowledge, teaching Tamsin the roads. Final beat: inheritance redefined — not what we're given, but what we refuse to pass on.
